descriptionChirho: The physical mouth of a person or animal, used for speaking, eating, or as the organ of speech; includes all pronominal and prepositional inflections where the referent is the literal mouth.
The cutting edge or blade of a weapon, especially in the idiom 'by the mouth/edge of the sword' (lefi cherev); Arabic hadd, Korean kalnal, Swahili makali, Hindi dhaar.
Idiomatic prepositional use meaning 'according to,' 'in proportion to,' or 'as befits'; Arabic hasab, Korean ttara, Swahili kulingana na, Hindi anusaar.
Metonymic use where 'mouth' stands for the authoritative utterance, command, or decree that issues from it; Arabic amr, Korean myeonglyeong, Swahili amri/neno, Hindi aajnaa/vachan.
The mouth or opening of a well, sack, cave, or other container; Arabic fathah, Korean ipgu, Swahili shimo/mlango, Hindi mukh (contextual).
The end or far edge of a physical extent; Arabic taraf, Korean kkeut, Swahili upande, Hindi chhor.
A proportional share or measured fraction of something; Arabic di'faani/thulthaa, Korean bae, Swahili sehemu/fungu, Hindi bhaag.
The opening at the neck of a robe or garment through which the head passes; Arabic fam (garment context), Korean otgit, Swahili ukingo/shingo, Hindi gale.
A unit of weight equal to approximately two-thirds of a shekel, used as a price for sharpening tools; a distinct lexeme that shares the consonantal form.
